q: The concept of lines of force was introduced by _____ as an aid in visualizing an electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The concept of lines of force was introduced by Michael Faraday as an aid in visualizing an electric field. Charles-augustin de coulomb or isaac newton is not this quantity.

q: Electric lines of force do not really exist; they are only _____ lines.
e: Electric lines of force do not really exist; they are only imaginary lines. Physical or magnetic is not this quantity.

q: An electric line of force is a path along which a small _____ charge will move in an electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. An electric line of force is a path along which a small positive charge will move in an electric field. Do not trade positive for negative or neutral.

q: The electric lines of force in an electrostatic field are continuous lines which start from a _____ charge and end on a negative charge.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The electric lines of force in an electrostatic field are continuous lines which start from a positive charge and end on a negative charge. Do not trade positive for negative or neutral.

q: Around a single positive charge, the electric lines of force are directed radially _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Around a single positive charge, the electric lines of force are directed radially outward. Do not trade outward for inward or parallel.

q: The electric lines of force are close together when the electric field intensity is _____ and far apart when the electric field intensity is small.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The electric lines of force are close together when the electric field intensity is large and far apart when the electric field intensity is small. Do not trade large for zero or negative.

q: Electric lines of force never intersect because the electric field intensity at any point can have only _____ direction.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. Electric lines of force never intersect because the electric field intensity at any point can have only one direction. Two or infinite is not this quantity.

q: The electric lines of force around two equal unlike charges start from the positive charge and end on the _____.
e: Like charges push apart. The force arrows point outward along the line joining them. The electric lines of force around two equal unlike charges start from the positive charge and end on the negative charge. Positive charge or infinity is not this quantity.

q: Electric lines of force will terminate on negative charges situated at _____.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. Electric lines of force will terminate on negative charges situated at infinity. The origin or the centre is not this quantity.

q: The concept of electric lines of force helps in _____ an electric field.
e: Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q. The concept of electric lines of force helps in visualizing an electric field. Do not trade visualizing for calculating or eliminating.

q: The electric lines of force around two equal positive charges show that the lines _____ each other.
e: Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The electric lines of force around two equal positive charges show that the lines repel each other. Do not trade repel for attract or intersect.

q: The density of electric lines of force represents the _____ of the electric field.
e: Density is mass per unit volume, ρ = m/V. The density of electric lines of force represents the intensity of the electric field. Do not trade intensity for direction or potential.
